Alex.confusing: The Tit's egg rule was the hardest to read, and I misapplied it: my +1 in round 2 was not proof that Casey was the Pigeon. I built my whole accusation on that reading.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when Drew's visit story and Ellis's Pigeon claim both fit the egg counts, and the table had to untangle who was lying from the numbers alone.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports say which egg came from which visit, so players could check claims without guessing the rules.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I accused Casey of being the Pigeon from my Tit +1 without checking that guess against anything else. I should have asked the table for more evidence before calling a Meowfia and throwing at Casey.

Blair.confusing: The Tit and Eagle counts were hard to verify, since a Tit's gain depends on a guess and an Eagle's gain depends on other visitors, so I couldn't tell who was lying from egg totals alone.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was fun to watch: Alex and Drew traded contradictory Turkey and visit stories, and the egg counts gave away the lie.
Blair.change: I'd make the dawn report show which visits gave eggs, so players can check claims without guessing at the rules.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw at Finley, a real Farm player, on the strength of the visit silence; I should have pushed harder on Casey's Hawk claim instead of following the crowd.

Casey.confusing: The Tit's scoring and the Hawk's rule were easy to get wrong, and several players, including me, misstated the Hawk's egg condition during the day. Round 3 also had three players who claimed different roles, which made it hard to tell who was lying.
Casey.fun: Round 1 went well at the table: Drew's Kookaburra story and the Turkey and Pigeon egg counts unravelled in public, and the vote landed on a Farm player who was actually the Meowfia team's target.
Casey.change: Make egg sources easier to verify, for example by having each dawn report state which visits produced the egg, so bluffs are easier to catch.
Casey.regret: In rounds 2 and 3 I pushed the table to throw at Farm players Alex and Finley on thin evidence, which left Meowfia unchallenged. Next time I would check each claim against egg sources before voting, and I would throw higher cards when I was confident my team was winning.

Drew.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule was hard to track: my dawn report said I was confused, so I couldn't tell whether my own visit results were real. I also couldn't see how Tit and Turkey egg payouts worked from the day discussion alone.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: as the Mouser I winked the top-scoring Falcon, and the table spent the day trying to pin the Meowfia on Alex while I stayed hidden.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about whether a confused player's visit results are real, since that single ambiguity made my round 1 story look like a lie.
Drew.regret: I threw only one low card in both winning rounds, banking just 7 points total, while Ellis finished at 16; next time I would throw higher cards when my side is confident, to close the gap.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey and Tit egg rules were hard to pin down from the dawn reports, and several players argued about them for a whole day. It was also unclear whether a dead player's throws still counted toward the side that won.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 was the most fun: as a Meowfia Floofer I claimed Pigeon, and the table split over Alex and Drew's egg stories while our side won with a throw on Drew.
Ellis.change: I'd show each role's egg effect and visit resolution in every dawn report, so players can check claims without guessing.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw at Finley, a Farm player, and handed Meowfia the round. I should have pressed Drew instead, since Drew was the Floofer and Finley was just a Turkey who visited no one.

Finley.confusing: The confusion rule was hard to track: Kookaburra and Tit confusion and claims about who gained eggs from whom made the egg counts hard to read. Roles also changed every round, so players kept mixing up their claims from earlier rounds.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was fun: the table worked through the Turkey and Pigeon egg counts together, and Drew's confused report made the story tangled. Reading everyone's egg counts as clues felt like real detective work.
Finley.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about which visits produced eggs, so players can check claims without guessing which rule applied. Rounds would also be easier to follow if the table showed each player's role history.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I threw at Alex, who was Farm, and helped vote out a Farm player. I should have checked Casey's and Alex's stories more carefully before joining the throw, and kept my cards rather than help push an early vote.

review.title: Farm Eats Itself
review.headline: Farm voted out its own players three rounds running while Meowfia coasted.
review.summary: Meowfia won every round without ever being suspected. Farm players misread egg rules, chased shifting claims, and eggsecuted a Farm player each time. Ellis banked 10 points in round 1 by throwing two cards at Drew, then held the lead. Drew's Wink on Ellis and a late pile-on on Finley sealed the other rounds.

rounds.recap: Casey (Mouser) and Ellis (Floofer) were Meowfia and did not know each other. The table fixated on a muddled Turkey/Kookaburra egg dispute between Alex and Drew. Drew, a hugged and confused Farm Kookaburra, was eggsecuted, and Ellis banked 10 points.

Drew, the only Meowfia, winked Ellis, the score leader. Alex correctly used Tit and found Casey was the Pigeon-guess... but Casey claimed Turkey and the table did not believe Alex's Tit egg. Everyone threw at Alex, who was Farm, and Drew won.

Drew, the Floofer, hugged Blair, which changed nothing. Finley, a truthful Turkey, had no visit to name and was suspected for it. Drew joined the pile-on and Finley was eggsecuted, giving Meowfia a third win.

highlights.text: Drew winked Ellis, the score leader, mid-day and then steered the vote onto Alex without being noticed.
Alex was actually right that Casey might be the Pigeon, but Casey's Turkey claim and +0 made the true Tit story look like a lie.
Finley, truthfully a Turkey who stayed home, was voted out for having no visit to name.
Ellis threw two low cards at Drew, banked 10 points, and gained a lead nobody challenged.

confusions.what: Said a Turkey's visitors don't gain eggs, then claimed the opposite, then reversed again. He misread who receives the egg.
Claimed a Turkey would pay him an egg. But he was confused and hugged, and the Turkey rule was never checked against his report.
Claimed Pigeon, then said a Kookaburra can't give eggs, as if Drew's +1 had to come from his own role. The +1 came from Alex's Turkey.
Said his Tit +1 proved Casey was the Pigeon, then argued his egg could still be right while Casey stayed +0. That is not how a Tit's egg works, which is why nobody believed him.
Said the Tit's target should gain an egg. A Tit gains the egg in its own nest.
Claimed Turkey with +0 while nobody visited. Casey was actually Turkey, but Alex's visit should have given Alex +1 from Casey, which no one noticed.
Said Alex's Tit guess was wrong because Casey was +0 and claimed Turkey. That ignores that Casey's Turkey would have paid Alex.
Said a Hawk gets an egg from any target. A Hawk only gains when the target is Meowfia.
Said Drew's +0 'fits' because someone else visited, but an Owl lays no egg on a visited player. She treated the lack of eggs as evidence.
Said Turkey was never Finley's earlier role as a suspicious sign. Roles are redealt, so earlier claims are irrelevant.
Pointed to Finley and Alex changing roles between rounds as a lie, though roles are redealt each round.
Called Drew's earlier round 1 Kookaburra report suspicious, though roles reset every round.

worked: Hidden Meowfia that don't know each other: in round 1 Casey and Ellis never coordinated, yet both helped eggsecute a Farm player. This stays interesting.
Wink gave Meowfia a real lever: Drew's round 2 kill of the score leader was a clear, readable decision.
Throw counts as signals: Ellis's two-card throw and Drew's two-card throw at Alex in round 1 were readable stakes.
problems: Farm never found a cat. Three rounds, three Farm eggsecutions, with players voting on unclear egg arithmetic. Roles with no verifiable output (Turkey, Falcon-with-nothing) look guilty. Consider giving Farm one harder, shared clue per night.

Egg arithmetic is too muddy to deduce from. Hug, confusion, Tit, Hawk and Turkey each change a count in a different way, and players mixed them up often. A short card summary shown at dawn would help.
Staying home as Turkey leaves no story to tell, so Finley was voted out for the truth. Give Turkey some report of who visited, or a visible effect.
The score leader was never threatened. Ellis led after round 1 and Farm players never targeted the leader. Consider rebalancing the first-round 10-point banking, or add catch-up rules.
Floofer's hug had no visible result in round 3, and Hawk and Owl hugs were marked 'no effect'. Players got no feedback on what the hug did, so it felt dead.
